title: Pipelined rerank executor with graceful token throttling
creator: Samira Patel
description:
Problem: The reranking endpoint shows unstable tail latency and suboptimal throughput for long candidate sets (50-500 candidates) due to head-of-line blocking and wide variance in token lengths across candidates. Current single-stage batching frequently forces worst-case token budgets across the entire batch, which increases P95/P99 latency and makes autoscaling reactive rather than predictive.

Goal: Implement a pipelined executor for rerank that decouples candidate tokenization/embedding from scoring, adds graceful per-request token throttling, and enables intra-request parallelism for scoring. This will reduce tail latency, increase steady-state throughput, and provide deterministic timeouts that bound user-facing latency while preserving quality.

High-level approach:
1) Stage pipeline: split work into (A) candidate tokenization & prefix trimming, (B) embedding / KV reuse, (C) scoring & final aggregation. Each stage will use small per-stage microbatches to reduce head-of-line blocking.
2) Token budget and graceful throttling: add a per-request token budget with two modes: strict (hard cap) and graceful (soft cap + quality-aware truncation). Graceful mode attempts to preserve highest-signal tokens using a heuristic (query-aware prefix selection) before truncation.
3) Parallel scoring: allow multiple scorer threads to operate on disjoint candidate subsets within a request; use non-blocking queues between stages to permit overlapping work.
4) Dynamic batching: implement a microbatching scheduler that adapts to request size distribution and changes the microbatch window to optimize P99 vs throughput trade-offs.
5) Fallbacks and safety: for requests hitting budget/timeouts, return partially-ranked results plus a quality flag and metric to the Console. Provide automatic fallback to a smaller, faster model when deadlines are tight.

Trade-offs considered:
- Complexity in correctness: ensuring deterministic ordering and stable scores across partial execution. We will preserve deterministic sorting by attaching full-score fallbacks computed in the final aggregation step.
- Quality vs latency: graceful throttling may prune some tokens; we will validate against held-out eval sets to bound quality loss to <=1% NDCG@10.
- Resource fairness: prioritizing per-request latency may reduce aggregate throughput; microbatch scheduler will expose knobs to tune for customer tiers (dedicated vs hosted).
acceptance_criteria: P99 latency improvement for standard 200-candidate workloads: reduce from baseline by >=25% in hosted 8-GPU cluster tests
Median throughput (requests/sec) for 100-candidate workloads increases by >=15% on the same hardware profile
Quality regression on rerank eval set: NDCG@10 drop <= 1% when graceful throttling enabled
Endpoint exposes token_budget and throttling_mode parameters; documented in API and SDK
Automatic fallback to fast-rerank variant implemented and observable in Console (flag + metric)
Comprehensive load test run in pre-prod with canary rollout plan and rollback criteria defined

comments: 2026-02-25 Samira: Created ticket after last week's incidents where a single 500-candidate request spiked the P99 to 3.2s. Initial notes from on-call attached.

2026-03-01 Diego: Implemented prototype pipeline in runtime branch 'eng/22501-pipeline'. Early microbenchmark: P99 reduced by ~18% for 200-candidate synthetic workload, but we observed a small (0.6%) NDCG dip with naive truncation.
2026-03-02 Maya: Ran offline evals against rerank-prod-holdout. Graceful truncation with query-aware prefix selection recovers quality; NDCG@10 delta now 0.3%.

2026-03-04 Patrick: Profiling indicates CPU scheduling between tokenization and scoring causes occasional stalls at high concurrency. Proposal: pin scoring threads to separate cores and increase queue depth to smooth bursts.
2026-03-06 Lia: Added metrics: rerank.stage_latency_ms, rerank.throttled_requests, rerank.fallback_count. Instrumentation PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/1248
2026-03-08 Design review (Olivia): API surface looks good; asked for backward-compatible defaults and explicit opt-in for graceful mode. Document changes required in SDKs.
2026-03-09 Diego: Performance run on pre-prod (8xA100) canary: P99 improved 26% on 200 candidates, throughput +18%. Next: add canary rollout steps and failure thresholds.
2026-03-10 Samira: Updated acceptance criteria to include API exposure and Console observability based on design review feedback. Scheduling canary for 2026-03-15.
